text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Consultants hired by the economic planning and development ministry to assess the viability of public loan disbursement schemes, have admitted there are inaccuracies in their draft report.
- Tribalism has hit a secondary school in Mzimba district in northern Malawi causing resentment among teachers and the community.
- Information and broadcasting minister, Brown Mpinganjira, said he is determined that television services will be introduced in the country within three months, even without the backing of donors.
- The current working relationship between the Civil Servants Trade Union and its members offered the government liberty to frustrate efforts to implement salary increases.
- The Malawi police force said its officers had received wage increases from January 1, but declined to say how much.
- Malawi needed to create an ethical environment to close loopholes for fraud and corruption, a lecturer at a seminar for the Society of Accountants said.
- Zambia's national soccer team, preparing for an Africa Cup of Nations match in Malawi, vacated a Blantyre hotel this week after an unidentified woman, thought to be from Zambia, said it was cursed.
- Home affairs minister, Wenham Nakanga, has defended his ministry in a row over if it was responsible for the rehabilitation of Malawi nationals deported from South Africa.
